introduccion.texto: Welcome to Bootcamp Genesis. I'm Jair: software engineer, thirty years old, late salary. And from today, your instructor.
Here you'll learn Coffee, the language of GENESIS. It looks like JavaScript, but with more coffee and less dignity.
The bootcamp's promise: from zero to developer in a few weeks. The actual result: burned-out developer, overweight and prone to type 2 diabetes. It's in the fine print.
I'll be helping the instructor. A warrior must master every art. Even the ones that come with coffee.
And I'm here to watch. The code, Jair, Rikka… especially Rikka when she bends over to plug in her laptop.
There's an outlet at desk height, Cami!
i came because the ad said “guaranteed employability”. it also said “snacks”. i suspect they lied twice
…and because you're the one teaching. but don't put that on any diploma
There's an AI assistant in the IDE: GENESIS. Don't use it. Not because it's cheating: because it never works.
While you solve the exercises I'll be there, in a corner, with them. Unfortunately. Let's begin.

resenas.texto: I went in knowing nothing and came out knowing I know nothing, but with a diploma. 10/10.

The graduates are good, but they ask to be paid. They didn't teach them to stop doing that.

🚀 From barista to developer in 12 lessons. I'm still a barista, but now I can write a for loop. #Mindset
In my day you learned by reading 900-page manuals and crying. Now it's all little stars.
I learned async/await. Now I wait for answers from 40 companies at once, without blocking the main thread (my anxiety).
At 71 I learned what a bug is. It was what my pension system had. Thank you.
